name: Register Variation Analysis
description: Analyzes the text for natural fluctuations in linguistic register (formality, tone, and stylistic appropriateness). Human writers naturally adapt their register depending on the context—shifting from academic presentation to conversational anecdotes, or from objective reporting to emotional appeal. AI models, heavily influenced by safety-alignment and RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback), exhibit a stubbornly uniform 'helpful assistant' register. They maintain an unnaturally consistent tone from start to finish, rarely displaying the dynamic stylistic shifts typical of authentic human communication.
mechanism: The algorithm evaluates the text across multiple linguistic dimensions (e.g., informational vs. involved, narrative vs. non-narrative) based on Biber's multi-dimensional framework. It calculates a 'Register Volatility Score' by tracking how formality, personal pronoun usage, and emotional valence change across paragraphs. A human narrative will show organic crests and troughs in these dimensions (e.g., starting formal, becoming conversational, ending with an emotional plea). AI-generated content typically scores incredibly low on register volatility, producing a flat, homogeneous stylistic profile regardless of the subject matter's inherent intensity.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing opinion pieces, creative writing, and long-form essays where natural register shifts are expected as the author builds rapport with the reader.
strengths:
• Targets the structural consequences of RLHF fine-tuning, making it robust against simple prompt modifications instructing the AI to 'write casually.'
• Excellent at differentiating between a passionate human blogger and an AI mimicking a blog post.
limitations:
• Less effective on extremely formal, highly constrained documents (like legal contracts or academic abstracts) where even humans are forced into a uniform, rigid register.
• Requires texts of at least 300-500 words to establish a baseline and measure variation meaningfully.
parameters:
Analysis: Multi-dimensional Biber Profiling
Metric: Register Volatility Variance
Output: 0-100 Stylistic Homogeneity (AI Consistency) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 76-84% accuracy. Exceptionally strong when combined with Emotional Tone and Pragmatic Adequacy analysis.

references.title: Biber, D. (1995). Dimensions of Register Variation: A Cross-Linguistic Comparison. Cambridge University Press.
Biber, D. & Conrad, S. (2009). Register, Genre, and Style. Cambridge University Press.
